candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

Halie Fox

I am writing to express my interest in the UR Coordinator position with your organization. My experience includes obtaining and securing prior authorizations, gathering and presenting clinical information to insurance payors, supporting continued stay requests, coordinating peer-to-peer reviews, and preparing appeals for authorization denials. I have also collaborated closely with treatment teams and healthcare providers to monitor patient progress, review treatment goals, and support appropriate transitions between levels of care.
My professional background has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively with insurance representatives, medical reviewers, and clinical professionals while managing time-sensitive authorization requests and maintaining attention to detail. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, organizational skills, and commitment to quality care to your team. I am confident that my knowledge of utilization review processes, medical necessity criteria, and behavioral health services would allow me to make a valuable contribution to your organization.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications and experience align with your organization's needs.
Sincerely,
Courtney A. Glover

Hiring Manager

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

Bilingual Clinical Mental Health Clinician

Bilingual (English/Spanish) counselor with an MEd in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and supervised clinical training across community mental health, school, and outpatient settings. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. Having earned my master’s degree in Counseling for Mental Health and Wellness from New York University, I am looking to transition into a role that allows me to remain connected to the mental health field while utilizing my clinical knowledge, interpersonal skills, and passion for helping others in a different capacity.

Through my experience as a counselor, I have had the opportunity to support individuals and families as they navigate difficult and often overwhelming seasons of their lives. My responsibilities have included conducting intakes, building rapport with clients, gathering sensitive information, coordinating appointments, maintaining confidential documentation, and identifying individual needs. These experiences have strengthened my ability to navigate sensitive conversations with compassion, professionalism, and sound judgment.

What particularly interests me about this position is the opportunity to support adolescents and their families at the beginning of their mental health journey. I understand that reaching out for mental health services is not always an easy decision, especially for parents who are concerned about their child's well-being and may be unsure of what steps to take. I believe that the initial interaction a family has with a treatment provider can make a significant difference in how comfortable and confident they feel moving forward with care. I would love to be someone who helps make that process feel less overwhelming.

In addition to my clinical background, I bring strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and experience independently managing a caseload within a virtual setting. I am comfortable balancing multiple responsibilities, learning new systems, and communicating with individuals from various backgrounds.

While I am looking to make a career transition, I am intentional about pursuing opportunities that continue to align with my passion for mental health and serving others. I believe this position would allow me to utilize both my clinical understanding and administrative abilities while making a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents and their families.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, experience, and passion for helping others could contribute to the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Jayde Whitten

I’d want each caller to feel heard and to leave the conversation knowing what happens next and when they’ll hear from me again.

As a plant manager with Goodwill Commercial Services, I led a team of roughly 100 people and worked closely with supervisors, quality staff, and planners. When an issue needed attention, my job was to listen carefully, get the details right, and make sure someone followed through. Running a property services business has given me hands-on experience with the other side of that work. I answer inquiries, coordinate appointments, and track open items so the person who called can count on an update.

I’d bring those habits to your admissions team. I’m comfortable managing my own workload, and I understand how much depends on an accurate record and a timely callback. If a caller asks a question I can’t answer, I take responsibility for finding the right person and getting back to them. That’s the kind of follow-through I’d bring to both programs.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could support your team and the people who reach out for care.

Sincerely,
Tyler Gusmus

November 24, 2026

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

What drew me to this role was the opportunity to be the first person someone speaks to when they decide they need help. I understand that many of those calls happen on some of the hardest days of a person's life, and I believe my background has prepared me well for those conversations.

For six years, I worked in Emergency Medical Services, responding to people during medical emergencies, mental health crises, and situations involving individuals experiencing severe emotional distress. During that time, I learned how to remain calm under pressure, listen without judgment, communicate clearly, and help people navigate difficult circumstances. Some of the most important moments weren't medical at all. They were simply being able to connect with someone, earn their trust, and help them take the next step.

After EMS, I went on to build and operate my own restaurant business. Owning a business taught me how to manage people, solve problems, stay organized, and communicate with individuals from every walk of life. Whether helping a customer, supporting an employee, or resolving a difficult situation, I found that my greatest strength has always been working with people.

I am not applying because I am looking for just another job. I'm applying because this is one of the few opportunities I've come across that genuinely interests me. Helping people find resources, treatment, and support during difficult periods of their lives is meaningful work, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and background can contribute to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

James Theodoredis

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience and commitment to service to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am especially interested in contributing to a team that helps young people and their families take meaningful steps toward wellness and recovery.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to submit my application for the this position. While my professional background may not follow the traditional path into behavioral health services, my experiences working with dependent adults, combined with my natural desire to help, nurture, and support others, have prepared me with valuable skills that I believe would make me an asset to your organization.

During my time working with dependent adults, I found great fulfillment in helping individuals maintain their independence, dignity, and positive outlook on life. My responsibilities often required patience, empathy, sound judgment, and the ability to navigate challenging situations. I also utilized my Crisis Prevention Intervention (CPI) training to help de-escalate situations, provide reassurance, and maintain a positive and supportive environment, particularly while assisting individuals in the community.

I understand that individuals seeking mental health and addiction services are often reaching out during some of the most vulnerable moments of their lives. I believe that the first interaction can make a tremendous difference in whether someone feels heard, respected, and comfortable enough to take the next step toward receiving help. I would approach every interaction with compassion, professionalism, patience, and without judgment.

My diverse professional background has also strengthened my communication, organization, customer service, and problem-solving abilities. I am comfortable working independently, adapting to new technology, learning new procedures, and managing responsibilities in a remote work environment. Although I recognize that I have much to learn about the specific intake processes within behavioral health services, I am eager to receive training and bring a strong work ethic and genuine commitment to the role.

I am looking for more than simply another job. I am looking for an opportunity to contribute meaningfully to the lives of others and become part of an organization whose work makes a difference. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my compassion, life experience, and dedication to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and personal commitment to helping others could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,

Patricia Umscheid

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your commitment to providing specialized mental health treatment and support for adolescents and their families is something that resonates with me on both a personal and professional level.

As someone who spent much of their adolescence navigating various mental health treatment programs, I understand firsthand how meaningful the right care, guidance, and support can be during some of the most formative years of a person’s life. The people who contributed to my growth and well-being made a lasting impact on me, and I have carried a desire to pay that forward ever since. I would welcome the opportunity to become part of a team that can make that same difference in the lives of other adolescents and their families.

My background includes an Associate of Science degree, experience and training as a Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA), and a lifetime of personal exposure to the complexities of mental health and individualized care. Mental health has been a significant part of my family’s experiences, giving me a unique perspective on how deeply these challenges can affect not only individuals, but entire family systems. Through both personal experience and professional exposure to caregiving, I have developed a strong appreciation for patience, empathy, adaptability, confidentiality, and meeting people where they are rather than where others expect them to be.

I believe that my combination of lived experience, education, and caregiving background would allow me to bring a valuable perspective to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to contribute in a fully remote environment while remaining connected to work that has a meaningful, real-world impact. Whether supporting patients and families directly, assisting with administrative responsibilities, or helping ensure that individuals feel heard and supported, I would approach the opportunity with dedication and genuine care.

Ultimately, I am looking for more than just a position. I am looking for an opportunity to contribute to something I believe in. The support I received as an adolescent helped shape the person I am today, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to help make that kind of difference for someone else.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, perspective, and commitment to compassionate care could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Norman “Finn” Gilderman

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position for Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my educational background in psychology, counseling experience, administrative leadership skills, and passion for mental health and addiction recovery, I am confident in my ability to support adolescents and their families as they navigate the treatment admissions process.

I am currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in Addiction and Recovery Psychology at Liberty University, with an anticipated graduation date of May 2027. Following graduation, I intend to pursue a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling. My education has provided me with a strong foundation in psychological principles, substance use disorders, behavioral health, trauma, and evidence-based approaches to recovery.

Through my counseling internship with East Coast Believers Counseling Ministry, I have gained practical experience conducting client intakes, administering behavioral health assessments, assisting with treatment planning, maintaining confidential documentation, coordinating appointments, and supporting individuals and families experiencing emotional and behavioral challenges. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to communicate compassionately, establish rapport, recognize individual needs, and approach sensitive situations with professionalism and empathy.

Additionally, my current position as a Warehouse Manager at Sun Plumbing has allowed me to develop strong organizational, administrative, leadership, and problem-solving skills. I am experienced in managing competing priorities, maintaining accurate records, communicating with diverse individuals, and working independently in a fast-paced environment. I believe these transferable skills would contribute to my success in a virtual admissions setting.

I also have experience providing addiction recovery education within my community. I am particularly passionate about reducing the stigma surrounding mental health and substance use disorders and helping individuals overcome barriers to receiving appropriate care. I recognize that seeking treatment can be an overwhelming experience for adolescents and their families, and I would welcome the opportunity to provide compassionate guidance, reassurance, and support during this important transition.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support its work with adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. I am eager to continue developing professionally while making a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and families seeking treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my education, professional experience, and dedication to behavioral health align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Gretchen Palmer

candidates.cover_letter:
Hello Team!

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA) and Principles Recovery Center (PRC). With a Bachelor of Social Work specializing in Alcohol and Drug Counseling, direct clinical intake experience in substance use and mental health treatment, and hands-on work supporting youth and families, I am uniquely prepared to serve as a calm, compassionate first point of contact for individuals taking the critical step toward recovery. 

My background bridges both populations your sister programs serve (adult substance use and co-occurring care). During my clinical practicum at The Healing Place (Women’s Campus), I worked directly with individuals navigating Substance Use Disorders and mental health diagnoses. I conducted client assessments, helped develop care plans, co-facilitated Intensive Outpatient Program (IOP) sessions, and maintained timely, HIPAA-compliant documentation. This experience allows me to explain PHP and IOP levels of care in simple, reassuring language while accurately screening callers for clinical fit.   

As a Sensory Motor Coach at Brain Balance Coral Springs, I work closely with young children and their parents to navigate behavioral, emotional, and neurodevelopmental challenges. I understand how overwhelming it can be for a parent seeking help for their teen and know how to guide families with empathy, clarity, and structure. 

In addition to my clinical foundation, I bring proven self-direction in remote environments. Whether managing an independent online business from inquiry to fulfillment or maintaining confidential student progress databases, I thrive when managing my own workflow, following up consistently, and ensuring no inquiry goes unnotified. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical intake background, warm communication style, and organizational discipline can help connect families to the care they need at AWA.

Thank you for your time and consideration,
Ranique Vissey (5615421437, niquevissey@gmail.com)

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Admissions and Intake position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Master’s degree in Applied Behavior Analysis and a diverse background in behavioral health, crisis intervention, substance abuse support, and early childhood education, I bring a well-rounded understanding of behavioral and mental health needs, family support, and the importance of connecting individuals with appropriate care.

My professional experience includes working as a crisis, suicide prevention, and substance abuse hotline counselor, where I supported individuals experiencing emotional distress, mental health crises, and substance-related challenges. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate with individuals in vulnerable situations, assess immediate needs and safety concerns, practice active listening, and provide compassionate support while navigating sensitive conversations. I understand the importance of remaining calm, professional, and empathetic while helping individuals and families navigate difficult circumstances.

Additionally, my graduate education and BCBA practicum experience provided hands-on exposure to behavioral assessment, clinical documentation, data collection, and individualized treatment planning under BCBA supervision. My background in childcare and education has further developed my ability to build rapport with children and families, understand developmental needs, and communicate effectively with individuals from diverse backgrounds.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines my passion for behavioral health and supporting families with my strengths in communication, organization, and clinical understanding. I recognize that the admissions process is often a family’s first point of contact when seeking help, and I would value the opportunity to make that experience informative, compassionate, and welcoming.

I am detail-oriented, adaptable, and comfortable handling sensitive information, managing competing priorities, and working both independently and collaboratively. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my education, crisis support experience, and commitment to helping individuals and families to the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills align with the needs of your team.

Sincerely,
Jarryn Bowles

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. My professional background combines behavioral health, patient intake and admissions support, direct patient care, healthcare administration, and nearly seven years in financial services, including several years of fully remote work.

During my time at Tacachale, a state-operated residential developmental disability center under Florida’s Agency for Persons with Disabilities, I provided direct care to individuals with complex developmental, psychiatric, and behavioral health needs. In addition to my daily patient care responsibilities, I assisted with the admissions process, including completing admission-related paperwork and preparing residential accommodations for incoming patients. My experience also included behavioral de-escalation, multidisciplinary collaboration, and training more than 60 employees across multiple residential units.

In my current role with Baptist Health Care, I support patient intake, registration, appointment coordination, insurance authorizations, and communication between patients and clinical providers. I regularly navigate sensitive conversations, resolve patient concerns, and manage competing priorities while maintaining accurate documentation and patient confidentiality.

During my tenure with Navy Federal Credit Union, I was among the early employees to transition to a fully remote work environment at the onset of the pandemic and remained fully remote throughout the remainder of my employment. This experience strengthened my ability to independently manage my workload, navigate multiple electronic systems, maintain accountability, and consistently deliver exceptional service.

What particularly draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is how closely this opportunity aligns with my professional goals. I am currently pursuing my nursing degree with the intention of specializing in psychiatric nursing. I plan to continue working in behavioral health as a registered nurse while advancing my education to become a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner. Psychiatry is not simply an area of interest for me; it is the specialty in which I am committed to building my career.

I understand that seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience for adolescents and their families. I take pride in my ability to establish rapport, communicate with compassion, simplify complex information, and provide reassurance while helping individuals navigate their next steps.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, initiative, and genuine commitment to behavioral health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how I could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Ashley Okahara

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Mental Health Admissions position. With a background in victim services, administrative coordination, and client support, I bring a strong combination of interpersonal communication, organizational skills, and the ability to navigate sensitive situations with compassion, professionalism, and discretion.

In my current role as a Victim Compensation Coordinator with Victim Witness Services, I work closely with individuals who have experienced trauma and are navigating some of the most difficult circumstances of their lives. My responsibilities include communicating with clients, coordinating services, gathering and reviewing documentation, explaining program requirements, and working alongside community partners and other agencies to help individuals access the resources they need. This experience has strengthened my ability to approach difficult conversations with empathy while maintaining professionalism, confidentiality, and attention to detail.

I understand the importance of creating a welcoming and supportive experience for individuals who may be feeling overwhelmed, vulnerable, or uncertain about seeking help. I am comfortable managing sensitive information, coordinating multiple moving parts, communicating with diverse populations, and ensuring that administrative processes are handled accurately and efficiently. I believe these skills translate directly into the admissions process, where compassion, responsiveness, and organization are essential.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed a reputation for being dependable, adaptable, and committed to helping others. I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to continue working in a service-oriented capacity while contributing to an organization that helps individuals access mental health treatment and support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and commitment to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely, 
Bailee Brown

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear hiring team,

I'm writing to apply for the remote virtual admission coordinator role at Adolescent Wellness Academy. When a family finally decides to reach out for help for their teenager, it's never really easy and usually overwhelming. That first conversation matters deeply and I would love the chance to be a calm, compassionate, and reliable first point of contact for the families reaching out to AWA.

Part of why I feel so drawn to this work is deeply personal. Having navigated my own mental health challenges and spent time in group therapy settings, I know firsthand how intimidating it is to ask for support. I was met at where I was in my journey and it was life changing to be heard with genuine support, judgement-free. That lived experience isn't something I bring into conversations to center myself but rather something that grounds how I listen. It helps me meet anxious parents and struggling teens with genuine patience, warmth, and respect right where they are. 

Professionally, my background has always been centered on building trust and helping people feel comfortable in unfamiliar spaces as well as the administrative sides of admissions. As a registered behavior technician, I worked closely with Board Certified Behavior Analysts to support clients and families while maintaining ethical, confidential communication and accurate session documentation. Before that, my time as an office administrator gave me hands-on experience serving as a welcoming concierge, verifying applicant details, auditing records for accuracy, and keeping daily data entry organized. Alongside my current work as a creative workshop facilitator and instructor, my background in being operations and studio support, I've spent years welcoming nervous newcomers, explaining next steps clearly, and coordinating schedules and logistics smoothly.

I admire AWA's whole-family, judgement-free approach to mental health care and I would be grateful for the opportunity to help families take that very first step towards healing. Thank you so much for your time and consideration. I'd love the chance to speak with you about how I can contribute to your admissions team.

Warmly, 
Anna K. Betts

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I’m excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. Throughout my career, I’ve had the opportunity to work in sales, recruiting, leadership, and business operations, but the part I’ve always found most rewarding is working with people and knowing that the work I’m doing is making a difference.

I’m looking for an opportunity where I can bring my experience, work ethic, adaptability, and genuine care for people to a team that values making a difference. I’m confident in what I have to offer, but I’m also someone who is always willing to learn, grow, and take on new challenges.

I hope everyone is ready to enjoy a long weekend, spend some time with loved ones, and give thanks.  I am grateful for the opportunity to apply for the role of Virtual Admissions Coordinators: Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment.

My resume is a little cut and dry, however, I hope to hear from you so that we can discuss my 19 years of customer service, many of which were spent 1 on 1 doing intake, scheduling, accurate data entry, or my journey through recovery  and my want to give back. Through working at a truly amazing salon with inspiring educators and business women, I quickly learned how easily the first person a client talks to can set the tone for the entire relationship - that my role and demeanor is the first impression- for this role not only of the Adolescent Wellness Academy, but of recovery.  I am welcoming, friendly, empathetic, and genuinely want to help in any way that I can. I have been on the other end of those phone calls, and that gives me the unique experience necessary for this role that goes beyond administrative skills (although I have those, too). 

As someone who has been where most of these people are calling from, I am already proud to talk to anyone who had the courage to stop digging and pick up the phone. I have 6 years (consecutively!) of sobriety and am active in the AA community. I am actively sponsored, sponsor other people in the 12 step program, and am active on the bid committee for WINDYPAA (the bid to bring the annual Illinois State Conference of Young People’s AA) to Chicago in 2028. I care deeply for my fellows and anyone trying to crawl out, and I would be honored to give back. 

I have all of the qualifications posted, and then some that I have picked up along my way. I have the necessary phone skills to direct a caller to stay efficient, while being helpful and compassionate and not robotic or demanding. I can learn any system, and am a leader or team player depending on what is more helpful in that moment. I know the importance of teamwork and find joy in working with others. Again, I just want to be helpful, and that is apparent in the way I show up for my team and my clients. 

If you have any questions at all about my experience, my background, my technical skills, or if you would like any references please do not hesitate to reach out. I would truly look forward to the prospect of giving back what was given to me, I already respect you all so much and would love the chance to join your team. 

Thank you for the opportunity, I hope everyone has a wonderful Thanksgiving, and I hope to hear from you soon,

Jen LaGioia

candidates.summary:
Hello, my name is Jen and I am applying for the role of Virtual Admissions Coordinator. I offer a combination of more than 15 years of professional administrative/intake experience and personal insight into the recovery process, bringing both the practical capabilities and human understanding this position requires.

My professional background includes healthcare scheduling and coordination, remote work, patient communication, and extensive one-on-one client relations. I have experience managing schedules, coordinating appointments, communicating with patients and families (Surgical Intake and Discharge), maintaining confidential records(Hospital Intake), and navigating sensitive situations with professionalism, patience, and compassion. I'm comfortable working independently (All State), managing competing priorities(Hair Colorist, Surgical Intake and Bed/Nurse Assignment, Server), and following through to ensure people receive the information and support they need.

I also bring a personal understanding of the recovery and treatment process. I have six years of sobriety and remain actively involved in the AA community. I am sponsored and sponsor other women in recovery as well as participating  in the bid committee working to bring the Illinois State Conference of Young People's AA Conference to Chicago in 2028. Having personally experienced treatment, including IOP and hospitalization, I understand what it can feel like to be on the other end of the phone, people are calling after they have been through the ringer. Somewhere I have been, somewhere my parents have been, my sponsees have been, their parents have been. They are scared, uncertain, vulnerable, and looking for someone who will listen without judgment, and looking for help sometimes for the very first time. 

That perspective has given me a deep appreciation for how important the first interaction can be. I understand that an admissions coordinator isn't simply scheduling an appointment, they're often helping someone take a difficult but important first step. In this role I understand that it will likely be a parent or family member who is dealing with the weight of their loved ones future being at risk. I already am so proud of anyone that can do that.  I would bring empathy, discretion, strong organizational skills, and respect and knowledge for the recovery process to this role. I have the administrative and client relation hard skills that make me an excellent fit for this role, and the life experience and soft skills to excel at it. I'm excited by the opportunity to help individuals and families get the help they need, make them feel supported in a scary/emotional time, and confident that they are on the right track by making the call.

Gabriel Cruz
Jacksonville, FL | 904-891-1129 | gabriel139242@gmail.com

Dear Hiring Team,
I'm excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. This role combines the two things I care about most: helping people through a hard moment and making sure they never feel alone in it.
For nearly 11 years I lived with addiction, so I know what it feels like to be afraid, ashamed, and unsure whether help is real. I'm now sober, and I've spent that time working the steps and taking part in NA, AA, and SA. One of my deepest goals, and a prayer I return to often, is to be a light for others the way people were for me. When I read that your callers reach out on one of the hardest days of their lives, I knew this was the kind of work I want to do.
I also have professional experience speaking with people in crisis. Since 2019, I've worked with Kanner & Pintaluga as a Personal Injury Intake Specialist, where I reach out to clients who have been hurt in accidents and are often frightened and overwhelmed. My job is to listen, calm them, and reassure them that help is here and that things will be okay. I conduct 10 to 15 recorded statements a week and explain next steps clearly. I also know how to initiate claims, verify information, and keep accurate records. Before that, at US Legal Services, I conducted client intake interviews, matched people with the right services, and followed up with in-network providers.
Here is what I would bring to your team:
Calm, compassionate phone presence with callers and families in vulnerable moments
Intake and follow-through: gathering information, coordinating next steps, and staying with a case until it is resolved
Insurance knowledge: I'm a licensed all-lines adjuster with years of experience reading and working with insurance information
Bilingual English and Spanish, so I can serve Spanish-speaking families in their own language
Lived experience and understanding of recovery, which helps me explain treatment in plain, caring terms and earn trust quickly
Independence: I manage my own caseload and deadlines without daily direction
I would welcome the chance to learn more about the role and talk about how I can support your callers and your team. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Gabriel Cruz

Melanie Q. Kartawinata

questionnaire.response: My supervisor would say my most significant area for growth was learning to slow down and double-check my documentation in a high-volume environment, and why that mattered. Early on, I was very focused on speed and getting through my queue quickly to help as many families as possible. My supervisor pointed out that when I rushed, I was more likely to miss a small detail in eligibility notes or intake paperwork, and in admissions, even one small error can delay care for a family. That feedback helped me change my process. I learned to pause, review my notes before submitting, and confirm coverage details before moving to the next case. It made me more accurate and organized, and it ultimately helped families get admitted faster because there were fewer errors to fix later.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team, 
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. What initially drew me to this opportunity was the chance to combine my experience in healthcare, client communication, and administrative coordination with work that has a meaningful impact on individuals and families. 

In my current role as a Client Care Manager, I work directly with clients and families to complete intakes, explain available care services, and help guide them through the process of getting the support they need. I also handle a variety of administrative responsibilities in a hybrid and remote work environment, which has strengthened my ability to stay organized, communicate effectively, and manage responsibilities independently. 

Previously, I worked in health insurance, where much of my role involved speaking with individuals over the phone and helping them understand their policies, coverage, benefits, and available options. I learned how important it is to take information that can often feel confusing or overwhelming and explain it in a way that makes people feel informed and comfortable. That experience taught me to listen carefully, ask the right questions, and meet people where they are, rather than simply providing information and moving on. 

My background in the restaurant industry has also played a significant role in developing my communication and interpersonal skills. Working with people from all walks of life taught me how to build rapport quickly, navigate difficult conversations, and remain patient and personable in fast-paced environments. 

Most importantly, as a Sociology graduate, I have always been interested in understanding people, their experiences, and the circumstances that shape their lives. I am especially drawn to opportunities where I can use that understanding to help others navigate important moments and access the support they need. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an emotional and sometimes overwhelming experience for families, and I would approach those conversations with patience, compassion, and genuine care. 

I would love the opportunity to bring my experience, communication skills, and enthusiasm for helping others to your team. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the chance to speak with you further about the position. 

Sincerely,
Annie Gaspard

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background in crisis intervention, survivor-centered advocacy, child welfare, behavioral support, and customer service, I bring a compassionate, organized, and trauma-informed approach to supporting individuals and families navigating difficult circumstances.

During my time as an Adult Advocate with Women in Distress, I provided crisis intervention, risk assessments, safety planning, and individualized advocacy to survivors of domestic violence. My responsibilities included connecting individuals with healthcare, counseling, housing, financial assistance, and other essential community resources. This experience strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, establish trust, maintain confidentiality, and help individuals navigate complex and emotionally challenging situations.

Previously, as a Case Aide with the Arizona Department of Child Safety, I supported case managers working with vulnerable children and families. Through trauma-informed support, documentation, resource coordination, and professional collaboration, I developed a deeper understanding of the challenges families face when accessing services and navigating systems of care.

In my current roles as an Educational Support Staff Assistant and Afterschool Lead Teacher at Great Hearts Academies, I provide individualized behavioral, academic, and social-emotional support to scholars with diverse needs. I work collaboratively with educators, special education professionals, and families to promote safety, emotional well-being, and positive development.

Additionally, my extensive customer service and leadership experience with Starbucks has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, resolve concerns, communicate effectively, and remain composed in fast-paced environments.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to helping adolescents and families access meaningful mental health treatment. I understand that reaching out for help can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience, and I believe the first interaction with a treatment provider should be compassionate, respectful, and reassuring.

I am eager to apply my transferable skills to admissions coordination, client screening, referral management, documentation, and consistent follow-up. I am also committed to expanding my knowledge of behavioral health admissions procedures, insurance verification, electronic medical record systems, and partial hospitalization and intensive outpatient programs.

My commitment to advocacy, combined with my professional experience supporting vulnerable populations, would allow me to contribute meaningfully to both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for considering my application. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and passion for helping others align with your organization’s mission.

Sincerely,

Candice Brooks

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With experience in healthcare operations, patient admissions, intake coordination, insurance verification, referral management, and care transitions, I am confident in my ability to provide compassionate and organized support to individuals and families navigating the admissions process.

In my current role as a Home Infusion Intake Specialist with Texas Health Resources, I coordinate referral-to-start-of-care processes, review clinical documentation, identify and resolve intake barriers, verify insurance benefits, and coordinate prior authorizations and payer follow-up. I also communicate with patients regarding financial responsibility and work closely with nursing, pharmacy, sales, and physician teams to ensure patients can move forward with timely care. This experience has strengthened my ability to manage multiple referrals, maintain accurate electronic records, and protect confidential patient information in accordance with HIPAA requirements.

Previously, as a Territory Patient Admission Coordinator with AccentCare, I coordinated admissions and care transitions between hospital and home-based settings while communicating with patients, families, and healthcare providers. I prioritized caseloads and urgent needs and maintained consistent follow-up to support continuity of care. My additional experience as a Patient Care Coordinator and Medical Office Representative further developed my skills in patient inquiries, scheduling, insurance authorizations and verification, electronic health records, and cross-functional healthcare coordination.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of the importance of being a compassionate and dependable first point of contact for individuals and families seeking treatment. I understand that reaching out for behavioral health or substance use treatment can be a difficult and vulnerable moment, and I would bring a calm, respectful, patient-centered approach to every interaction. I am also comfortable managing detailed workflows independently, communicating across multiple teams, and ensuring that referrals and documentation continue moving forward until the appropriate next step is identified.

While my background has primarily been in broader healthcare and home-based care settings rather than behavioral health admissions specifically, my admissions, intake, referral, payer, and patient coordination experience provides a strong foundation for this role. I am eager to apply those skills in a behavioral health environment where compassionate communication and reliable follow-through can make a meaningful difference.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare operations and patient services experience could contribute to the admissions teams at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over six years of experience in the mental and behavioral health field, a bachelor's degree in Psychology, and ongoing graduate studies in Marriage and Family Therapy at Capella University, I am passionate about supporting adolescents and their families as they navigate emotional, behavioral, and relational challenges.

Throughout my professional career, I have gained valuable experience in crisis intervention, psychiatric care, applied behavior analysis, behavioral health assessments, and patient advocacy. In my current role as a Crisis and Access Specialist with Protocall Services, I provide compassionate support to individuals experiencing mental health crises through risk assessments, de-escalation, safety planning, and connection to appropriate resources.

Previously, as a Senior Psychiatric Technician with Atrium Health, I worked alongside multidisciplinary healthcare professionals to support individuals experiencing acute psychiatric and behavioral health concerns. These experiences have strengthened my ability to establish rapport, navigate challenging situations, communicate effectively, and provide individualized support while maintaining a safe and therapeutic environment.

As a Marriage and Family Therapy graduate, I am continuing to develop my clinical skills in therapeutic interventions, emotional regulation, family dynamics, and treatment planning. I have a particular interest in working with children and adolescents and helping them develop healthy coping strategies, strengthen their self-esteem, build resilience, and establish meaningful relationships.

I am drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy's commitment to providing comprehensive, compassionate, and family-centered mental health treatment. Your emphasis on supporting adolescents through structured therapeutic services aligns closely with my professional interests, personal values, and long-term career goals.

I believe my diverse behavioral health background, clinical training, adaptability, and commitment to professional growth would make me a valuable addition to your team. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your organization while continuing to make a meaningful difference in the lives of adolescents and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to further discuss how my experience, education, and passion for mental health align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Afua Woods

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in joining your team in a remote position supporting adolescents and
families navigating mental health and substance use challenges.
I bring nearly 10 years of experience as a Home Consultant with Riverview Homes, where I work closely
with customers, listen to their needs, explain options, solve problems, coordinate details, and guide them
through what can sometimes be a complicated process. This experience has strengthened my
communication, organization, patience, and ability to build trust with people from different backgrounds.
In addition to my customer-facing experience, I have an extensive background in healthcare, including
working as a Resident Coordinator, Certified Nursing Assistant, and independent Home Health Care
Provider. These roles taught me the importance of compassion, dependability, confidentiality, and treating
every individual with dignity and respect.
I also have a personal understanding of the impact addiction can have on individuals, families, and
communities. Having lost people close to me to addiction, including my son, I recognize how deeply these
struggles affect everyone involved. This experience has strengthened my belief in the importance of
accessible treatment, early support, and making sure individuals and families feel heard rather than judged.
Although my professional background has been in healthcare support and customer consulting rather than
adolescent behavioral health, I believe my combination of healthcare experience, communication skills, and
personal understanding would allow me to bring empathy and dedication to this role. I am comfortable with
Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, and Teams, and I am confident in my ability to learn new systems and
processes.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience
and commitment to helping others could contribute to your organization.
Sincerely,
Stacey Kingsley

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am comfortable balancing multiple responsibilities, collaborating with colleagues, and recognizing the importance of both efficient administrative processes and meaningful human connection.

Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your mission and supporting the patients and families who rely on your services.

Warm regards,

Jorge Ruiz

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Human and Community Advocacy from the University of Texas at San Antonio, an Associate of Arts in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare, customer service, and public assistance, I bring a combination of professional qualifications, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping adolescents and families access mental health services.

Throughout my career, including my work with Texas Health and Human Services, healthcare-related call centers, and my current position with Aflac, I have developed strong skills in communication, active listening, documentation, problem-solving, and assisting individuals through complex and sometimes emotionally challenging situations. My experience has taught me the importance of maintaining confidentiality, gathering accurate information, explaining processes clearly, and ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported.

What makes this opportunity particularly meaningful to me is my personal experience as a mother who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for a child experiencing significant emotional and behavioral health challenges. I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to mental health advocacy would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jermiane Rodriguez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager, 

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a background in mental health services, clinical work, and program support, I bring a combination of administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills that align well with the responsibilities of this role. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate the process of accessing mental health and substance use treatment during what can often be a difficult and overwhelming time.

In my previous role as a Program Support Specialist within Post-Release Services, I developed experience supporting program operations, coordinating services, maintaining documentation, and communicating with individuals and various service providers. This role strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain organized records, facilitate communication, and ensure that important follow-up tasks were completed. Additionally, my clinical experience has provided me with familiarity with electronic health record systems, timely and accurate documentation, client scheduling, and the importance of maintaining confidentiality and HIPAA-compliant practices.

As a mental health professional, I understand the importance of approaching individuals and families with empathy, patience, and clear communication. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be a vulnerable first step, particularly for adolescents and their families. I would bring a compassionate, nonjudgmental approach to initial inquiries while maintaining the organization, consistency, and attention to detail necessary to support an effective admissions process. I am also comfortable navigating conversations that require balancing sensitivity with clear communication, follow-through, and appropriate coordination of services.

Although my background has primarily been in clinical and program support settings rather than a dedicated admissions role, I believe these experiences have equipped me with highly transferable skills. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical perspective, administrative capabilities, and commitment to accessible mental health care to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skill set could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Stephanie Lee-Ferreira

Vanessa Rincon, B.S., CBHCMS
Miami, Florida

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With over seven years of experience in behavioral health, mental health services, substance use treatment, and care coordination, I bring a strong understanding of the importance of making individuals and families feel supported, informed, and comfortable when navigating treatment options.

Throughout my career, I have worked closely with individuals experiencing mental health and substance use challenges, coordinating referrals, facilitating access to services, communicating with families and providers, and helping clients navigate the treatment process. In my current leadership role as a Social Services Manager, I oversee case management operations and work closely with clinical teams to ensure timely referrals, appropriate service coordination, accurate documentation, and compliance with HIPAA and regulatory requirements.

My experience has provided me with a strong foundation in referral management, intake coordination, insurance-related processes, follow-up, and maintaining accurate records within electronic health record systems. I am comfortable managing multiple priorities, communicating with individuals during difficult situations, and ensuring that inquiries do not fall through the cracks. I also understand the importance of explaining treatment options in a clear, compassionate, and approachable way.

I am bilingual in English and Spanish, highly organized, and comfortable working independently in fast-paced environments. I am also familiar with behavioral health documentation systems and technology, and I adapt quickly to new CRM and EMR platforms.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to combine my behavioral health experience with direct admissions support, helping individuals and families take the first step toward receiving the care they need. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your admissions team and support the continued growth of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and background can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Vanessa Rincon, B.S., CBHCMS

Dear Hiring Team,

I recently applied for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position and wanted to share why this work
matters to me. When a parent calls about mental health or substance use treatment for their teen, they
may be worried and unsure where to start. I’d like to be the person who listens, explains the next step
clearly, and follows through on what I said I would do.

At True North Pediatrics, I helped families with patient intake, scheduling, referrals, and insurance
verification. I kept patient records up to date and followed up when information was missing. As a
Child Protective Investigator with the Florida Department of Children and Families, I spoke with
children and caregivers during difficult circumstances and documented sensitive information with
care. Both roles taught me how much it matters to stay calm, ask clear questions, and make sure
families know what happens next.
I’m fluent in English and Spanish, and I’ve supported clients by phone, email, and video. My studies in
forensic psychology and my training as a Christian Mental Health Coach have deepened my interest in
how families navigate the decision to seek help.

I’d bring that perspective to your admissions team along with the practical habits I’ve built in pediatric care: keeping track of referrals, protecting confidential information, and following up when a family is waiting for an answer.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to talk with you about how I can support your admissions team and the families who reach out to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Lizmar Encarnacion-Rosario

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, ongoing graduate studies in Social Work, and professional experience in behavioral health intake, case management, and substance use support, I bring a combination of clinical understanding, administrative coordination, and compassionate communication. As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am especially passionate about helping individuals and families overcome barriers to accessing mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Case Manager at EMC Behavioral, I work in a fully virtual environment, supporting children and adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. My responsibilities include conducting intake assessments, identifying service needs, verifying insurance, coordinating referrals, scheduling appointments, and maintaining accurate client documentation. Working remotely has strengthened my ability to independently manage my responsibilities, communicate effectively with clients and caregivers through virtual platforms, and ensure timely follow-up without requiring daily in-person supervision. I understand the importance of maintaining confidentiality, accurate documentation, and consistent communication when coordinating behavioral health services remotely.

Additionally, as a Bilingual Parent Support Specialist at Catholic Charities' Guadalupe Home, I support young mothers experiencing various challenges, including substance use concerns, in a residential shelter environment. My work involves providing trauma-informed support, assisting with behavioral and emotional challenges, communicating with residents, and maintaining accurate documentation. Working with individuals during vulnerable periods has taught me the importance of approaching difficult conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel respected and supported.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because both programs serve populations with whom I have direct professional experience. I understand that individuals and families seeking behavioral health or substance use treatment may feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or afraid. I believe that providing clear information, listening without judgment, and following through on next steps can make a meaningful difference in their willingness and ability to access care. My experience with insurance verification, intake coordination, appointment scheduling, and client communication, combined with my ability to work independently in a fully remote environment, aligns closely with the responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health experience, organizational skills, and bilingual communication abilities to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background can support your programs and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Jennyfer Alvidrez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. With over 10 years of experience in healthcare and senior care, along with a strong background in patient coordination, admissions, scheduling, insurance authorizations, and customer service, I believe I can make a valuable contribution to your team.

Throughout my career, I have developed strong communication and organizational skills while working closely with patients, families, healthcare providers, and insurance companies. My experience includes coordinating patient admissions, managing referrals, verifying insurance authorizations, handling sensitive information, answering inquiries, and ensuring that individuals receive timely assistance and appropriate support.

I hold certifications as a Certified Nursing Assistant, Medical Assistant, and Psychiatric Technician. These qualifications, combined with my hands-on healthcare experience, have given me a strong understanding of patient needs, confidentiality, compassionate communication, and the importance of treating every individual with dignity and respect.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because I value helping individuals and families navigate challenging situations and access the care they need. I am confident in my ability to manage virtual admissions inquiries, communicate effectively with families, coordinate with clinical teams, and help facilitate a smooth admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare background, administrative experience, and commitment to compassionate patient care could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,
Maria Gabriela Morales
